title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 06
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An unconformity represents:
options: A continuous sequence of sedimentary deposition
A gap in the geological record due to erosion or non-deposition
A fault cutting through sedimentary beds
A change in the dip of strata
questions.solution: An unconformity is an erosion surface or period of non-deposition separating two sequences of rock, representing a gap in geological time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the dip of a coal seam is 30° and a borehole is drilled at 45° to the dip direction, the apparent dip of the seam in the borehole plane is:
questions.solution: Apparent dip in borehole direction = tan⁻¹(tan30° × cos45°) = tan⁻¹(0.5774 × 0.7071) = tan⁻¹(0.4082) ≈ 22.2°. Using sin relation: sin(app dip) = sin30° × sin45° = 0.5 × 0.707 = 0.354, app dip ≈ 20.7°. Closest answer is 21.2°.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The purpose of 'plunge' in structural geology is:
options: To measure the depth of a borehole
The vertical angle that a fold axis or lineation makes with the horizontal
The angle of dip of a fault plane
The slope of a haul road
questions.solution: Plunge is the angle between a linear feature (fold axis, lineation) and the horizontal plane, measured in the vertical plane containing the line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a borehole log, the 'core recovery' is defined as:
options: The ratio of core diameter to borehole diameter
The percentage of actual core recovered compared to the total length drilled
The time taken to recover the core
The depth at which core is recovered
questions.solution: Core recovery = (length of core recovered / length drilled) × 100%. It indicates the quality of drilling and ground conditions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A reverse fault is formed due to:
questions.solution: Reverse faults are caused by compressional tectonic forces that push the hanging wall upward relative to the footwall.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The bearing of a fault line measured along the fault plane intersection with a horizontal surface is called:
questions.solution: Fault strike is the bearing of the line formed by the intersection of the fault plane with a horizontal surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A coal seam is intersected in a vertical borehole at 200 m depth. A second vertical borehole 200 m away along the dip direction intersects the same seam at 310 m depth. The dip of the seam is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of geological unconformity?
questions.solution: The three types of unconformities are angular, disconformity, and paraconformity (nonconformity). 'Lateral unconformity' is not a standard classification.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In borehole surveying, the magnetic survey method is unreliable when:
options: The borehole contains steel casing or is near mineralized zones
questions.solution: Magnetic surveys are affected by steel casing, drill rods, and magnetic mineral deposits which deflect the compass readings.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'heave' of a fault is defined as:
options: The horizontal displacement measured perpendicular to the fault strike
The total displacement along the fault plane
The width of the fault gouge
questions.solution: Heave is the horizontal component of fault displacement measured perpendicular to the strike of the fault.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A syncline is a fold in which:
options: The oldest rocks are in the core
The youngest rocks are in the core
Both limbs have the same dip direction
questions.solution: In a syncline, the youngest rocks occupy the core (center) of the fold, and the limbs dip toward the axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the true thickness of a coal seam dipping at 40° is 2.5 m, the thickness measured perpendicular to a vertical borehole would be:
questions.solution: Apparent thickness in vertical borehole = true thickness / cos(dip) = 2.5 / cos40° = 2.5 / 0.766 ≈ 3.26 m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The process of correlating coal seams between boreholes involves:
options: Matching lithological and palaeontological features to establish continuity
Determining the age of coal by carbon dating
questions.solution: Borehole correlation uses lithological characteristics, fossil content, and seam properties to establish the continuity of strata between boreholes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A monocline is a fold where:
options: Both limbs dip in opposite directions
One limb is horizontal and the other is inclined
The fold has an axis that plunges
All limbs dip toward the center
questions.solution: A monocline is a step-like fold with one horizontal limb and one inclined limb, resembling a draped blanket.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In dip and strike determination from borehole data, a minimum of how many boreholes are needed if the seam is assumed planar?
questions.solution: Three non-collinear points (boreholes) are required to define a plane and determine its dip and strike uniquely.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'termination' of a borehole is recorded at the final depth. If the borehole is terminated in a coal seam, the seam is described as:
questions.solution: When a borehole ends within a coal seam, it is said to have 'bottomed in' that seam.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A fault where the dip of the fault plane is less than 45° and the hanging wall has moved up is classified as:
questions.solution: A thrust fault is a reverse fault with a low dip angle (typically less than 45°), formed under compressional stress.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The primary purpose of mine plans is to:
options: Provide accurate spatial information for safe and efficient mining operations
Serve as decorative displays in offices
questions.solution: Mine plans are essential documents that provide spatial data for planning, safety, and regulatory compliance in mining operations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'plan' in mine surveying is a:
options: Horizontal representation of the mine at a particular level
questions.solution: A plan is a horizontal projection of mine features at a particular elevation or level.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The standard scale for an opencast mine general plan is typically:
questions.solution: General plans of opencast mines are typically prepared at scales of 1:1000 or 1:2000 for operational use.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'section' in mine surveying represents:
options: A horizontal slice of the mine
A vertical slice through the mine showing elevation changes
A diagonal cut through the mine
questions.solution: A section is a vertical representation showing the mine features in elevation, typically along a specific line of cut.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Mine Plans and Sections' rules under CMR 2017 require that plans be kept updated at intervals not exceeding:
questions.solution: Under CMR 2017, mine plans and sections must be updated at intervals not exceeding six months or as prescribed by the Chief Inspector.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'elevation' or 'profile' of an opencast mine shows:
options: Vertical view along a particular line showing bench heights and slopes
questions.solution: An elevation or profile shows the vertical representation of mine features along a specific line, displaying bench heights and slope angles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The responsibility for preparation and maintenance of mine plans primarily rests with:
questions.solution: The surveyor is responsible for preparing, maintaining, and updating mine plans and sections as per statutory requirements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Contour plans are used to represent:
options: Surface topography with lines of equal elevation
questions.solution: Contour plans show lines of equal elevation, representing surface topography and地形 of the mine area.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In an opencast mine plan, the 'dump level' is represented by:
options: A closed contour at the top of the dump
questions.solution: The top of a dump is represented by a closed contour at its elevation, with the dump boundary shown by the outermost contour.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The colour convention for representing coal seams on mine plans is typically:
questions.solution: By convention, coal seams are represented in black on mine plans, while other features use different colours.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'section' drawn perpendicular to the face of an opencast bench shows:
options: The bench height, face angle, and overall slope angle
The geological map of the area
questions.solution: A face section shows the vertical profile of the bench including bench height, face angle (angle of working), and overall slope angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Coal Mines Regulations 2017, the plan of an opencast working must show:
options: All workings including past and present, with dates
questions.solution: Regulations require that plans show all past and present workings with dates, along with other essential features.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The storage of mine plans must ensure they are:
options: Available at the mine office and preserved for a prescribed period
questions.solution: Mine plans must be stored at the mine office and preserved for the period prescribed by regulations, typically for the life of the mine plus a specified period.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'longitudinal section' of an opencast mine shows:
options: A vertical view along the length (usually along the strike) of the mine
A plan view at a particular level
questions.solution: A longitudinal section is a vertical representation drawn along the length of the mine, typically parallel to the strike of the working face.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The scale of a mine plan should be selected based on:
options: The size of the mine area and the detail required
questions.solution: Scale selection depends on the mine area size, level of detail required, and regulatory requirements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'barrow' or 'cross-section' of an opencast mine bench at right angles to the face shows:
options: Only the top of the bench
The bench geometry including height, width, and slope angles
The plan view of the bench
questions.solution: A barrow/cross-section perpendicular to the face shows the complete bench geometry for operational and safety assessment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The preservation period for mine plans as per Indian coal mine regulations is typically:
questions.solution: Mine plans must be preserved indefinitely or for the period prescribed by the Chief Inspector, as they are permanent records.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a mine plan, the working face of an opencast mine is represented by:
questions.solution: The working face is typically represented by a thick solid line on mine plans to clearly indicate the current position of extraction.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'contour interval' on a mine plan refers to:
options: The distance between two adjacent contour lines
questions.solution: Contour interval is the vertical difference in elevation between two adjacent contour lines on the plan.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The surveyor's duties include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.solution: The surveyor is not responsible for operating mining machinery. Their duties include setting out, planning, volume measurement, and plan maintenance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a mine section, the 'overall slope angle' is:
options: The angle of a single bench face
The angle formed by a line joining the crest of the top bench to the toe of the bottom bench with the horizontal
The angle of the haul road
The dip of the coal seam
questions.solution: The overall slope angle is the angle of the line connecting the top crest to the bottom toe, encompassing all benches and berms.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'dump plan' in opencast mining shows:
options: All dumps — past, present, and planned — with levels and slopes
Only the haul roads leading to dumps
Only the geological features under the dump
questions.solution: Dump plans show all dumping areas with their levels, slopes, boundaries, and progression over time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The statutory requirement for mine plans is specified in which regulation?
questions.solution: CMR 2017, Regulation 116 deals with the preparation and maintenance of plans and sections of mines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'profile' of a dump or highwall is prepared to show:
options: The vertical outline and slope angles at a specific location
questions.solution: Profiles show the vertical outline of dumps or highwalls at specific cross-sections for stability assessment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When preparing a plan of an opencast mine, the surveyor must ensure that the plan shows:
options: All surface and subsurface features including boreholes, faults, and boundaries
questions.solution: Comprehensive mine plans show all relevant surface and subsurface features for safe and efficient operations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'bench map' of an opencast mine shows:
options: All benches in a single plan view
The plan of a particular bench at a specific level
A vertical section through all benches
questions.solution: A bench map shows the plan of a specific bench at a particular elevation, showing its contours, faces, and features.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a mine plan, an old working (goaf) is typically shown in:
questions.solution: Old workings or goaf areas are typically shown in blue with hatching to distinguish them from current and planned workings.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The preparation of a 'contour map' for an opencast mine involves:
options: Drawing random lines on the plan
Connecting points of equal elevation on the surface or bench
Drawing the boundary of the mine only
questions.solution: Contour maps are prepared by connecting points of equal elevation, obtained from survey observations, to represent the topography or bench surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The surveyor must ensure that mine plans are signed and countersigned by:
options: The surveyor and the mine manager
questions.solution: Mine plans must be signed by the surveyor who prepared them and countersigned by the mine manager as per statutory requirements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'composite plan' in opencast mining combines:
options: All benches at different levels superimposed on a single plan
questions.solution: A composite plan superimposes all bench levels on a single plan to show the complete mine layout at different elevations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'elevation' drawings of an opencast mine are useful for:
options: Assessing slope stability, bench heights, and overall mine geometry
questions.solution: Elevation drawings are critical for slope stability assessment, monitoring bench heights, and evaluating overall mine geometry.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In mine plans, the 'grid lines' represent:
options: A coordinate system (northing and easting) for referencing locations
questions.solution: Grid lines on mine plans represent the coordinate system (northing and easting lines) for precise referencing of locations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The mine plan should be updated and signed at intervals not exceeding:
questions.solution: As per CMR 2017, plans and sections must be updated and signed at intervals not exceeding six months.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'horizontal projection' in mine surveying refers to:
options: The projection of a point on a vertical plane
The projection of a point on a horizontal plane
The projection on an inclined plane
The projection on a cylindrical surface
questions.solution: A horizontal projection represents the position of a point as projected onto a horizontal reference plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The correct sequence for preparing a mine section is:
options: Draw contours → Plot survey points → Add annotations
Establish reference line → Plot levels → Draw section line → Add details
Mark boundaries → Draw grid → Add colours
questions.solution: The correct sequence is: establish a reference line, plot elevation levels along the section line, draw the section outline, and add geological and operational details.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A geological map primarily shows:
options: Only the topography of the area
The distribution of rock types and geological structures at the surface
questions.solution: Geological maps show the surface distribution of rock formations, their boundaries, and geological structures like faults and folds.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'V-rule' in geological map reading applies to:
options: Determining the dip of a bed from its outcrop pattern in valleys
questions.solution: The V-rule states that the outcrop of a dipping bed in a valley forms a V-shape pointing up-dip (for beds dipping upstream) or down-dip.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, the symbol for a sandstone is typically:
questions.solution: Sandstone is typically represented by a dotted pattern on geological maps.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An anticline on a geological map can be identified by:
options: Older rocks in the core with younger rocks on the limbs
Younger rocks in the core with older rocks on the limbs
Parallel bands of the same age
A single rock type covering the area
questions.solution: An anticline has older rocks in its core (center) with progressively younger rocks on the limbs.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A geological section is drawn by:
options: Projecting surface features onto a horizontal plane
Projecting surface features along a line onto a vertical plane
Drawing a plan view at a particular elevation
questions.solution: A geological section is a vertical representation of geological features projected along a section line onto a vertical plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'normal fault' on a geological map is indicated by:
options: Teeth on the upper side of the fault line
Tick marks on the downthrown side of the fault
Both sides having the same rock type
questions.solution: Normal faults are shown with tick marks on the downthrown side, indicating the direction of displacement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In geological map reading, a 'monocline' appears as:
options: A series of parallel bands with a change in dip direction
questions.solution: A monocline appears as a step-like change in dip, shown as a narrowing of outcrop bands in one direction.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'fold axis' on a geological map represents:
options: The line connecting the hinges of a fold at different levels
questions.solution: The fold axis is the line connecting the hinge points (points of maximum curvature) of a fold at different elevations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, coal seams are typically shown in:
questions.solution: Coal seams are shown in black on geological maps, often with a specific symbol or fill pattern.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'apparent thickness' of a bed measured on the surface perpendicular to the strike is:
options: Always greater than the true thickness
Always less than the true thickness
Equal to the true thickness if the bed is horizontal
questions.solution: The apparent thickness equals the true thickness only when the bed is horizontal. For dipping beds, it is always greater.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'syncline' on a geological map is identified by:
options: Youngest rocks in the core with older rocks on the limbs
All rocks being the same age
A sharp boundary with no gradual transition
questions.solution: A syncline has the youngest rocks in its core with progressively older rocks on the limbs.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'reverse fault' on a geological map is indicated by:
options: Tick marks on the downthrown side
Teeth/triangles on the upthrown side of the fault line
questions.solution: Reverse faults are shown with teeth or triangles on the upthrown (hanging wall) side.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, an unconformity is represented by:
options: A wavy or irregular line separating two sequences
questions.solution: An unconformity is shown as a wavy or irregular line on geological maps, indicating an erosion surface between two rock sequences.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'key bed' or 'marker bed' in geological correlation is:
options: A distinctive, easily recognizable bed used for correlation across areas
The thinnest bed in the sequence
questions.solution: A marker bed is a distinctive, laterally persistent bed (like a coal seam or volcanic ash) used to correlate strata across different locations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'dip and strike' symbol on a geological map shows:
options: The direction and amount of dip, along with the strike
questions.solution: The dip and strike symbol shows both the strike direction (long line) and the dip direction and angle (short perpendicular line with angle).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a geological map, if the contour lines and outcrop pattern of a bed form a 'V' pointing upstream in a valley, the bed is dipping:
options: In the direction of the valley
Opposite to the direction of the valley (upstream)
questions.solution: According to the V-rule, when the V points upstream, the bed dips in the upstream direction (opposite to valley flow).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'true thickness' of a dipping bed can be calculated from surface measurements using:
questions.solution: True thickness = apparent width × cos(dip) when the apparent width is measured perpendicular to the strike.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, a 'strike-slip fault' is shown by:
options: Horizontal offset of beds with no vertical displacement marks
questions.solution: Strike-slip faults show horizontal offset of beds without the vertical displacement indicators (tick marks) used for dip-slip faults.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'cross-section' in geology is different from a 'longitudinal section' in that:
options: Cross-section is drawn along the strike; longitudinal section is perpendicular to strike
Cross-section is perpendicular to the strike; longitudinal section is along the strike
questions.solution: A cross-section is drawn perpendicular to the structural trend (strike), while a longitudinal section is drawn along the strike.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Borehole correlation on a geological map involves:
options: Measuring the borehole diameter at each depth
Matching similar rock types and seam characteristics between boreholes
questions.solution: Correlation involves identifying and connecting equivalent rock units and coal seams between boreholes based on their lithological and palaeontological characteristics.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, the 'limb' of a fold refers to:
options: The planar portions on either side of the fold hinge
questions.solution: The limbs are the planar or gently curved portions of a fold on either side of the hinge zone.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A geological map showing 'contouring' of a coal seam surface would help in determining:
options: Only the boundary of the mine
The shape, dip, and structure of the coal seam surface
questions.solution: Contouring of a coal seam surface reveals its three-dimensional shape, including dips, folds, and structural features.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'outcrop pattern' of a horizontal bed on undulating topography appears as:
options: Lines that follow the contour lines of the topography
questions.solution: A horizontal bed outcrops along lines of equal elevation, so its outcrop pattern follows the topographic contour lines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a geological map, 'facies change' refers to:
options: A change in the dip of beds
A lateral change in the character of a rock unit
A fault cutting through the sequence
questions.solution: Facies change is the lateral variation in lithology, fossils, or other characteristics within a rock unit, indicating changing depositional environments.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'plunge' of a fold on a geological map is indicated by:
options: The convergence of outcrop bands in the plunge direction
questions.solution: As a fold plunges, the outcrop bands converge in the direction of plunge, creating a characteristic pattern.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, a 'dyke' is represented by:
options: A wide area of uniform colour
A narrow linear feature cutting across existing rock formations
questions.solution: A dyke is an igneous intrusion that cuts across existing rock layers, shown as a narrow linear feature on geological maps.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'principle of superposition' in geology states that:
options: The youngest rocks are at the bottom
In an undisturbed sequence, the oldest rocks are at the bottom and youngest at the top
All rocks are the same age
Igneous rocks are always older than sedimentary rocks
questions.solution: The principle of superposition states that in an undisturbed sedimentary sequence, the oldest beds are at the bottom and youngest at the top.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'graben' on a geological map is identified by:
options: An elevated block between two normal faults
A depressed block between two normal faults with younger rocks
questions.solution: A graben is a down-dropped block between two normal faults, showing younger rocks at the surface compared to the adjacent blocks.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Underground coal mining method 'Bord and Pillar' means:
options: A. Extracting coal from pillars only
B. Creating a grid of tunnels leaving coal pillars
questions.solution: In Bord and Pillar method, a grid of tunnels is cut leaving pillars of coal for support.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Act primarily governs mine safety in India?
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952 is the primary legislation governing mine safety in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The DGMS (Directorate General of Mines Safety) is headquartered in which city?
questions.solution: DGMS headquarters is in Ranchi, Jharkhand.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What does 'opencast mining' refer to?
options: B. Extracting minerals from surface deposits
questions.solution: Opencast mining involves extracting minerals from near-surface deposits by removing overburden.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: India's coal production target under Atmanirbhar Bharat was set at how many million tonnes by 2025-26?
questions.solution: India set a target of 1 billion tonnes (1000 MT) coal production.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act was enacted in which year?
questions.solution: CMSP Act was enacted in 2015 for transparent allocation of coal blocks.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which state is the second-largest coal producer in India?
questions.solution: Odisha is the second-largest coal-producing state in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Coal seam fire refers to:
options: A. Burning of coal at power plants
B. Spontaneous combustion of underground coal seams
D. Use of coal for cooking
questions.solution: Coal seam fire is the spontaneous combustion of underground coal deposits.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which scheme provides free cooking gas connections to BPL families?
questions.solution: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides free LPG connections to BPL families.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Digital India programme was launched in which year?
questions.solution: Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: PM-KISAN provides how much annual income support to farmer families?
questions.solution: PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments to farmer families.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which scheme aims to provide health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year?
questions.solution: Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY) provides health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on which date?
questions.solution: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 (Gandhi Jayanti).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Stand-Up India scheme provides loans to which category?
questions.solution: Stand-Up India provides loans to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Make in India initiative was launched in which year?
questions.solution: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which scheme provides electricity to all willing rural households?
options: C. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana
questions.solution: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) aims at universal household electrification.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Smart Cities Mission aims to develop how many smart cities?
questions.solution: Smart Cities Mission aims to develop 100 smart cities.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Atal Pension Yojana is aimed at which sector?
questions.solution: Atal Pension Yojana targets workers in the unorganized sector.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Skill India mission was launched in which year?
questions.solution: Skill India was launched on 15 July 2015.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which app was launched for transparent coal block allocation?
questions.solution: e-Coal portal was launched for transparent coal block allocation and monitoring.
